label: D-Latch (level-sensitive)

semantics.notes: Transparent latch: when EN=1, Q follows D continuously (transparent). When EN=0, Q holds. isSynchronous not set (undefined, assumed false). Verilog uses always@(*) with blocking '=' assignment — intentional latch inference. This causes Verilog tools to produce a latch warning, which is correct. Special const-propagation: if EN is const-1, generates assign (purely combinational); if EN is const-0, generates only a comment (holds init value).

exportSupport.verilogNotes: Normal: always@(*) begin if (en) begin q=d; q_n=~d; end end (latch inference). EN=const-1: assign q=d; assign q_n=~d; EN=const-0: comment only.
exportSupport.vhdlNotes: Normal: process(en, d) begin if en='1' then q<=d; q_n<=not d; end if; end process; EN=const-1: concurrent assign.

testability.notes: Test EN=1: Q follows D changes in real-time. Test EN=0: Q unchanged when D changes. Latch race-through: apply rapid D toggle while EN=1 (engine should handle via iterative evaluation). Test const-propagation: EN driven by CONST_HIGH or CONST_LOW.

risks.description: Latch race-through risk when EN is held HIGH for extended time — any glitch on D propagates directly to Q. Not an implementation bug but a model characteristic that tests should exercise.
Intentional latch inference in Verilog. Synthesis tools will flag this. This is correct behavior per the component specification, but users may be confused by tool warnings.
isSynchronous field not explicitly set on this gate definition. Default is undefined (falsy). STT and timing diagram may treat this as synchronous or combinational unexpectedly.

modelLimits: Hi-Z on D or EN treated as 0.
